summary: Round 2: every blocker and major finding from round 1 is fixed. Wire routes now follow the real load-free path (mast, ring_low +Y edge, down beside the +X yoke on two tie slots, across the roll pivot, along the ring top, across the pitch pivot, then the hub fork). They are machine-checked at home, at both ends of each gimbal axis and at the four corners against every part and prop disc. Cut lengths come from the worst pose, and the 66 g of wire is now counted in hover current, T/W (2.31) and mass (729 g). The rest is fixed too: the firmware path (ArduPilot CoaxCopter, PWM 1-2 motors / 3-4 servos in separate timer groups, MOT_SPIN_MAX 0.80) is stated with its residual risk; the dowels go in last from outside; the XT60 is on a grippable pigtail; the BOM additions (pad, capacitor, single 3 x 20 dowel row) are in. The mechanical side (sweeps, CG, tip-over, FEA load cases) is unchanged and sound; only minor documentation and BOM gaps remain.

findings.issue: The ArduPilot facts the flight depends on are only cited in DESIGN.md prose. They are not in the catalog entry or REFERENCES.md: board support, the PWM timer groups (1-2 / 3-4 / 5), CoaxCopter flap output functions 33/34 and motors 37/38, and MOT_SPIN_MAX. Whether the CoaxCopter flap mixer (which scales flap authority with throttle) steers a gimbal well is still unproven; it is correctly flagged as a risk.
findings.fix: Add an `ardupilot` block to drone.stacks.fc_20 with the hwdef/board-page URL and the timer groups. Add the CoaxCopter page to REFERENCES.md. Write the exact SERVOn_FUNCTION values (1=37, 2=38, 3/4=33/34 or as bench-verified) into WIRING.md.

findings.issue: The generated steps still say 'press the 3 x 20 mm dowel into ring_low / gimbal_outer' at the step where the part is fitted, without saying it goes in last and from outside. DESIGN.md steps 3 and 6 are correct, but a builder following ASSEMBLY.md alone could press the pin first and then be unable to hang the ring or hub.
findings.fix: Give pin sites an insert direction or order flag so ASSEMBLY.md says 'after the horn screws, press the dowel in from outside through <part>'. As a stopgap, add a note to the two steps.

findings.issue: All the gimbal-bound conductors cross the roll pivot as a single short span of about 23 mm, roughly 20 mm off the axis: 2 x 3 x 18 AWG plus the pitch servo leads, a bundle of about 8 mm. This span flexes every control cycle and adds torque that the 1.8 kg cm MG90S has to overcome. The cut length covers the stretch, but no geometry forces a real service loop.
findings.fix: After wiring, measure servo current (or check free movement by hand) at the four corners, as DESIGN.md already says. Make the crossing a U-loop of 30-40 mm hanging outside the yoke, tied on both sides, so the flex is spread out. Twist the motor triplets.

findings.issue: Several electrical rows still have no buy link: AWG 14 and AWG 24 wire, the low-ESR capacitor, the cable ties and the UBEC price. The brief asks for a buy link on every wire, connector and electrical part.
findings.fix: Add catalog/prices entries (with sources) for 14 and 24 AWG silicone wire, a 35 V low-ESR capacitor and 2.5 mm cable ties.

findings.issue: The pack's own XT60 lead must be at least 110 mm long, but CNHL does not publish its length. The mated XT60 pair also hangs free past the ring_top edge on a 14 AWG pigtail, so it will flop in flight and in a tip-over.
findings.fix: Measure the pack lead on arrival and record it in the catalog. Once plugged in, tuck the mated pair under the battery strap or tie it to the battery lead.

findings.issue: The support warnings are unchanged: motor_hub 24 %, ring_low 17 %, gimbal_outer 18 %, legs 20 %. The two upper pitch-horn M2 screws still need a ball-end key.
findings.fix: Optional: add 45 deg chamfers under motor_hub's disc where it meets the arm roots, and under the leg feet, to cut support. Keep the ball-end key note in step 6.

findings.issue: The micro 21T disc horn geometry is still an estimate, and the MG90S tab height has a 2.5 mm spread between sources. Both set the horn-face positions on gimbal_outer, motor_hub and ring_low.
findings.fix: Buy and measure the horn and servo before printing the three gimbal parts, update the catalog, and re-run kerf check.
